title: Show HN: Videolabs – narrated terminal-style courses
text:
I enjoy learning new tools watching videos on youtube of people showing their experiments, and sometimes i cannot find a good video explaining exactly what i need.

So i created this project to help me solve that problem.

Creating a video is one prompt, using claude skill to generate the video (@remotion + elevenlabs) and publishing into the page via cloudflare R2

the video script is tested by creating the lab in my local server, all commands/scripts/output is shared in the video page in case i need to verify something or copy the command ran in the video.

the whole project (website+ how to generate a new video) is in github https://github.com/bigzaqui/videolabs

This was my first weekend project with a single Claude Pro subscription, mind blown

title: Re: Show HN: FR/EN search engine built with Chez Schem...
text:
Everyone has their own challenge for generative AI. Mine was a search engine for about €150. A month or so later, here it is. Claude Code wrote most of the code; the architecture and storage layer are mine, built on years of earlier work. €150 is compute and storage at hetzner, and one month of claude pro max x5.

It needs polish here and there, but the results hold up, and some of its quirks surprised me in good ways. No ads, no tracking, no personalisation.

The corpus:

English (93M docs, 2.1 TB): Stack Overflow, arXiv, Wikipedia, Hacker News and Lobsters up to 2020

French (18M docs, 0.5 TB): theses.fr, Persée, Gallica, Wikisource, Wikipédia

How it’s built, since that’s probably the interesting part here:

Everything is Chez Scheme. The storage layer is an ordered key-value store (it implements SRFI-167/168, which I wrote) running as an LSM tree.

The C parts: libtls, liburing, picohttpparser, libc. French and English are separate indexes. Mixing them corrupted document frequencies in an earlier version, because French and English words collide after stemming.

Known weaknesses: ranking is the next big piece of work.

What would help most: a query where it failed you, or a source you think belongs in the corpus and why. I’m especially curious which corpora people would put in a “technical history” index.

The code isn’t public yet. I want to see what people actually use before I freeze the design.

There is json output: https://h9p3r.fr/?q=biological+intelligence+future+&lang=en&...

title: Show HN: Pi-cowboy – use Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode as subagents
text:
pi-cowboy is an agent orchestrator for Pi(https://pi.dev) and Herdr(https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr). Break large jobs into focused subtasks, hand them off to background agents running in parallel, and consolidate the results when they finish. Each agent runs in an isolated copy-on-write Git work-tree, minimising disk overhead.

pi-cowboy can orchestrate foreign harnesses too, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and more.

Feature highlights:

- Foreign harnesses: pi-cowboy agents can run in Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pig and Pi-Bolt, as well as Pi. This gives you great flexibility in choosing how to spend your tokens. Running out of Codex usage? Switch your pi-cowboy harness to OpenCode, select one of its free models, and let it handle the rest. Pig and Pi-Bolt are pi variants that are more efficient, with a lower memory footprint and faster performance than pi. Because pi-cowboy is designed to run multiple agents in parallel, having a lower per-agent footprint is crucial. It prevents your machine from running out of resources and lets you have higher concurrency without choking your system.

- Concurrency limits: You can configure concurrency limits at every level. Running a local model with limited resources? If a simple task already takes hours to complete, the last thing you want is to overload your machine by running too many of them at once. Set concurrency limits for that model specifically to keep resource usage under control.

You can install it on Pi as a package:

  pi install npm:pi-cowboy #(requires `herdr` 0.8+)

title: Show HN: A 3D catalog of rocket engines you can take apart
text:
Here you have 13 different rocket engine technologies, 9 have flown, 3 built and test fired, but not flown and 1 never completed.

I created this site because I wanted to learn more about rocket engines and how they work. My background is HVAC/plumbing engineer and 3D artist, not rocket engineer, so I built this just out of my personal curiosity.

Here you can investigate each motor type and learn what each part does, explode and cutaway the model and see how fuel and oxidizer flow to generate the thrust.

Site is created using Claude Opus 5.5. Claude made also the 3D models using Blender MCP. Site runs on Babylon.js 9.16.1 on WebGL2.

What I did was basically art direction and fact checking. It took me about one week, among other projects, to get this site finalized so that I was happy about the design and outcome.

Any improvements, corrections and comments are welcome!

title: Show HN: Parents Inbox – Communication Guide for Schools
text:
At a dinner party with other parents recently, the conversation turned to the challenges we all have with communication coming from our children's schools. Emails and Texts and App notifications, coming from Teachers, Admins, PTA, After-Care programs. Overlapping information, buried key details, verbose fluff. An avalanche of text every day that must be carefully parsed to find important info.

This seems to be a universal problem and certainly one I experience every day. So literally before dinner was over I built the first version of this site on my phone with Claude.

I think the main problem is that the folks who are responsible for communication just don't have the tools and experience to know what good communication really looks like, or the parents perspective hasn't been demonstrated to them to give them more empathy. So I am hoping this can help. Feel free to share if you have the same problem with your school.

title: Show HN: 500 clocks in one 6.3 MB HTML file by Opus 5.5
text:
